Higher = more faces linked per cluster (looser grouping, risk of mixing persons). Lower = only very similar faces linked (tighter clusters, more suggestions).
Higher = clusters are assigned to existing persons more easily (fewer new suggestions). Lower = only very similar clusters are merged with a person.
Higher = single faces are assigned to existing persons more easily. Lower = only very close matches are assigned (more faces land in Unknown).
Higher = only large groups become suggestions (fewer but more reliable). Lower = even small groups of faces become suggestions.

Controls how strongly time influences matching. Higher = temporally close photos of a person are preferred for matching, and photos far apart are less likely to be linked (helps with siblings and ageing). Set to 0 to ignore time completely.

Faces just beyond the auto-assign threshold become unconfirmed suggestions you can accept or reject. This margin is a fraction of that threshold: 0.10 means suggestions reach 10% past it. Lower for cleaner but fewer suggestions, higher to recover more borderline faces at the cost of more mixing.

Eidora detects and groups faces in your photos — entirely on your device, without any cloud. To do this it needs access to your photos.
Required to read and analyse your photos.
Required to write recognised names back into your photo files (XMP metadata), compatible with DigiKam and Aves.
How Eidora handles dates and metadata in your photo files.
Add a date to undated photos

Gallery apps sort your photos by their capture date — Eidora included. Most photos carry that date in their metadata — but some don't: screenshots, downloaded images, or photos that lost their metadata along the way.

For a photo without a capture date, gallery apps — Google Photos, your system gallery and others — fall back to the file's modification time to place it. The catch: when Eidora writes the faces it finds back into a photo, that modification time changes to "now" — and an undated photo jumps to the top of your timeline in exactly those gallery apps, as if it were taken today.

To prevent that, Eidora can write a capture date into such photos before it touches them, taken from the file's current modification time. This locks in their place in the timeline for good. This date-filling only affects photos that have no capture date yet — an existing capture date is never overwritten.

You can change this any time in Settings.
Recommended. Only undated photos are affected.
When a photo has no capture date, write one (from the file\'s modification time) so it keeps its place in the timeline even if the file is changed later. Only affects photos that have no date yet.
